policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'On that day went Jesus out of the house' opens a new section with no connective, but ASV routinely leaves a paragraph-initial de untranslated, so the English neither requires nor excludes the added particle.
ASV 'went ... out of the house' renders exelthon with 'out of' whether or not apo stands before tes oikias; no wording or note distinguishes the readings.
ASV reads 'he entered into a boat', anarthrous; ASV renders the articular to ploion as 'the boat', so the indefinite article follows the base reading without the article.

ASV 'and the birds came and devoured them' is coordinate, which suits the finite elthen/elthon ... kai, but ASV also regularly resolves an aorist circumstantial participle into a coordinate English clause, and 'came' does not distinguish singular from plural. Nothing in the verse or its notes settles it.
ASV 'choked them' renders epnixan and apepnixan alike; the apo- prefix has no separate English exponent here.

ASV text reads 'He that hath ears, let him hear' without 'to hear', and the mapped textual_variant note — 'Some ancient authorities add here, and in verse 43, to hear' — places the added akouein outside the text ASV rendered.
ASV 'And he answered and said unto them' renders the indirect object, so autois stood in the text; the omission is excluded.
ASV 'and your ears, for they hear' is plural, matching akouousin; the singular akouei would give 'it heareth'.
ASV 'the parable of the sower' is a substantival participle whose tense is not rendered in English; aorist speirantos and present speirontos are indistinguishable here.
ASV reads 'the care of the world' with no demonstrative; had toutou stood it would read 'this world'. The 'Or, age' note is an alternative_rendering about aionos and does not bear on the variant.
ASV 'upon the good ground' renders either word order; the variation is transposition and article placement only, with no English exponent.
ASV 'and understandeth it' renders sunieis and sunion alike — the same present participle in alternative spellings.

ASV 'a man that sowed good seed in his field' is past, matching the aorist speiranti; ASV renders the present participle of this verb as 'he that soweth' (v. 37), so the present speironti is excluded.

ASV 'sowed tares also among the wheat' has no kai in the clause to carry 'also', which therefore renders the epi- of epespeiren ('sowed in addition'); the simplex espeiren leaves 'also' unaccounted for.
ASV 'didst thou not sow good seed' renders espeiras and espeires alike; the variation is an orthographic ending with no English exponent.

ASV 'And the servants say unto him' names the servants, excluding r01 which lacks douloi, and uses the present 'say', excluding r03's aorist eipon. The remaining readings differ only in the order of douloi, auto and legousin, which the English does not register.
ASV 'Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?' renders the deliberative subjunctive sullexomen and the future sullexomen identically after theleis.
ASV 'But he saith, Nay' is present, matching phesin; the imperfect ephe would give 'he said'.
ASV 'until the harvest' renders mechri and heos alike; both are simply 'until' in English.
ASV 'Gather up first the tares' does not distinguish the aorist imperative sunagagete from the present sunagete; English imperatives carry no aspect here.

ASV 'and hid in three measures of meal' takes its 'in' from the following prepositional phrase, so the en- prefix of enekrupsen has no separate exponent and the simplex ekrupsen is equally rendered by 'hid'.
ASV 'without a parable spake he nothing unto them' renders a pronoun 'nothing', which is ouden; the bare negative ouk would give only 'spake he not'.

ASV reads 'hidden from the foundation of the world', rendering kosmou, and the mapped textual_variant note — 'Many ancient authorities omit of the world' — confirms the words stand in the text ASV translated.
ASV 'Then he left the multitudes, and went into the house' uses the pronoun; the added ho Iesous would give the named subject, as ASV supplies it elsewhere in the chapter (v. 34, 'spake Jesus').
ASV 'Explain unto us the parable' fits both Diasapheson and Phrason, which are near-synonyms for 'explain, make plain'; no note maps to the unit.
ASV 'And he answered and said, He that soweth' has no indirect object, so the added autois is excluded; ASV renders autois when present (v. 11, 'said unto them').
ASV 'the end of the world' renders the genitive with or without the article tou; English 'the' here belongs to the head noun and does not report the Greek article on aionos.
ASV 'burned with fire' takes 'with fire' from puri and gives no separate exponent for the kata- prefix; kaietai and katakaietai are alike rendered 'burned'.
ASV 'in the end of the world' has no demonstrative; the added toutou would give 'this world', as ASV renders the demonstrative where it stands.

ASV reads 'He that hath ears, let him hear' without 'to hear', and the note 'See verse 9.' points to the verse 9 textual note, which places the added akouein 'here, and in verse 43' among authorities ASV did not follow.
ASV v. 44 begins 'The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure' with no 'Again'; ASV renders Palin when it stands, as at v. 45 ('Again, the kingdom of heaven').

ASV 'selleth all that he hath' renders panta, excluding r01, which lacks it. The remaining readings differ only in whether polei precedes or follows panta hosa echei, which the English word order does not report.
ASV 'like unto a man that is a merchant' renders anthropo alongside emporo; the omission would give simply 'a merchant'.
ASV 'and having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold' is a coordinate clause with a participle, matching heuron de; the relative hos heuron would give 'who, having found ... went'.
ASV 'gathered the good into vessels' renders ange and angeia alike; the two are the same noun in alternative forms.
ASV v. 51 begins directly with the question, 'Have ye understood all these things?'; the added Legei autois ho Iesous would give 'Jesus saith unto them' before it, which ASV does not have.
ASV 'They say unto him, Yea.' ends without a vocative; the added kurie would give 'Yea, Lord', as ASV renders that vocative where it stands.
ASV 'made a disciple to the kingdom of heaven' fits both the bare dative te basileia and eis ten basileian, either of which ASV may render with 'to'.
ASV 'Is not this the carpenter's son?' renders the negative interrogative alike for ouch and the emphatic Ouchi; English marks no such emphasis.
ASV names the brother 'Joseph', which is Ioseph; the variant Ioses would be rendered 'Joses', a distinct name in ASV usage. The 'Or, Jacob' note concerns James and does not bear on this unit.

ASV 'save in his own country, and in his own house' gives a possessive to both nouns, but the base reading's single autou after oikia governs the pair, and ASV regularly renders an anaphoric article as 'his own' without marking a supply. The English does not require the added autou after patridi.
